scams.name: Athens Airport & Piraeus Cruise Port Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: After a long flight or a tiring ferry from the islands, the taxi queue at Athens International Airport feels like the easiest way to reach your hotel. You climb in, the driver nods at your destination, and by the time you arrive at Syntagma the meter reads €160. The legal flat rate from the airport to central Athens is €40 between 5 AM and midnight, and €54 at night — those prices are posted on signs at the taxi queue itself. r/GreeceTravel 'Was I fooled by this taxi driver? Paid 160 Euros' (comments/1ghxrhm) is a verbatim case; r/GreeceTravel 'Taxi scam at Athens airport — here is what worked for us' (comments/1sf346r, 2025) documents the official protection in detail. Piraeus cruise port is the other flashpoint, and r/GreeceTravel 'Another taxi ripoff' (comments/1lwfzxg) captures the pattern from a cruise passenger verbatim: 'Just got off a cruise ship and took one of the taxis lined up at Piraeus port for a half-hour ride to Neos Kosmos…' Cruise arrivals are perfect targets because passengers are often disoriented, carrying luggage, and under time pressure to reach their hotel or a connecting tour. Drivers use three variations: claiming the meter is broken and quoting a flat €80–€160; running a tampered meter that climbs unusually fast; or taking surface streets instead of the Attiki Odos motorway, which doubles the legitimate fare. In July 2025 Greek authorities arrested an Athens taxi driver specifically for overcharging tourists, with Greek City Times reporting the case as part of a broader enforcement push. That is reassuring, but the scam continues because the Tourist Police response is hours away from any given moment. The best protection is to bypass the queue entirely. From the airport, Metro Line 3 runs directly to Syntagma for €9 per person (40 minutes), and the X95 express bus runs for €6 (60 minutes). From Piraeus, Metro Line 1 reaches Monastiraki for €1.40 in about 20 minutes. If you do take a taxi, use Uber, Bolt, FreeNow, or Beat — all four apps work in Athens, show fixed prices before you commit, and provide a digital receipt. Your hotel concierge can also pre-arrange a fixed-price airport transfer for €45–€55.
scams.avoidance: From Athens Airport, use Metro Line 3 (€9, 40 minutes) or the X95 express bus (€6, 60 minutes) to bypass taxis entirely If you take a taxi, insist on the posted flat rate — €40 daytime or €54 overnight — and point to the sign at the queue Use Uber, Bolt, FreeNow, or Beat apps for all city taxi rides; app prices are fixed and receipts are digital Ask your hotel concierge to arrange a fixed-price airport transfer (€45–€55) before arrival for peace of mind If overcharged, photograph the taxi license plate and report to Tourist Police 171 — 2025 arrests have followed this process
scams.location: Athens International Airport (ATH) arrivals, Piraeus cruise port, Syntagma Square taxi rank

scams.name: Fake 'Skip-the-Line' Acropolis Ticket Websites
scams.description: You plan ahead. Weeks before your trip you search 'Acropolis tickets online' and click the first result — a site called acropolisticket.com, or a close variant. The design looks professional. You pay €45 per person for 'skip-the-line' tickets. At the Acropolis gate on arrival, the scanner beeps and the staff shake their heads: the QR codes are blank. r/GreeceTravel 'Skip the line tickets for Acropolis a scam' (comments/15e99j9) captures the exact site: 'Please avoid acropolisticket.com — the website is a complete scam and they send out fake passes!! I'm trying to resolve the issue with my bank…' The only official Acropolis ticket site is hhticket.gr (operated by the Hellenic Heritage company, which contracts with the Ministry of Culture). The on-site variant runs in parallel. Touts outside the Acropolis ticket booth and near the Theatre of Dionysus approach tourists in the queue with 'skip-the-line passes' for €25–€40 per person. These printed vouchers are either outright fakes that fail at the gate or are actual combination tickets resold at a markup. The real Acropolis combo ticket (which covers the Acropolis plus six ancient sites for five days) costs €30 from October to March or €20 for winter season in 2025, and is sold at the official Acropolis ticket booth, at any of the other sites in the combo, or on hhticket.gr. The Ministry of Culture and the Tourist Police (171) both publicly warn about unauthorized resellers. If you want a guided tour, book through a verified operator with printed credentials — recommended by r/GreeceTravel community threads are GetYourGuide, Viator, and local licensed guides displaying a yellow certification badge from the Greek Federation of Tourist Guides. Avoid any stranger approaching you near the ticket booth with a 'skip-the-line' offer, and verify your online ticket seller by searching the domain name plus 'scam' before paying. For older travelers: the climb to the Acropolis is steep and uneven; go early morning to avoid both heat and queues, and allow extra time.
scams.avoidance: Book online only via hhticket.gr (the official Ministry of Culture ticket site) or verified resellers GetYourGuide, Viator, Tiqets Search the domain name plus 'scam' before paying any online Acropolis ticket seller At the Acropolis entrance, buy tickets at the official booth next to the main gate — ignore anyone approaching you in the queue Licensed Greek tourist guides wear a yellow certification badge; ask to see it before hiring a guide on-site If you've already been scammed, dispute the charge with your credit card within 60 days for a full chargeback
scams.location: Online booking before arrival; touts selling printed vouchers outside the Acropolis entrance

scams.name: 'Friendly Local' Plaka & Monastiraki Bar Invitation
scams.description: You've finished a late afternoon walk through the Ancient Agora and you're sitting at a Plaka café enjoying the breeze. An older Greek man — warm, charming, speaking good English — strikes up a conversation. He loves meeting visitors and suggests you join him at 'a traditional ouzeri just down the lane.' The bar is dimly lit, tucked on a side street. He orders two ouzos. Forty minutes later he is ordering a round for 'his friends' who have joined the table, and when the bill arrives it is €240 for drinks you did not knowingly order. Two men at the door confirm you cannot leave until you pay. r/GreeceTravel 'Plaka, Athens — Old Man Ouzo Scam Still in Operation' (comments/1glmgzo) documents this exact script: 'George brought us to a brothel about five minutes from where we had been eating lunch, and we were charged €60 for four drinks.' The r/athina community posted a 2025 scam alert (comments/1p4xxby) detailing the escalation: a first round of ouzo-orange juice 'special' mixers for €10 each, then bar staff and 'ladies' order drinks for themselves that appear on your tab, with the total climbing to €200–€400 before bouncers move toward the exit. r/GreeceTravel 'Scammed today in Athens' (comments/x49o2k) shows the final stage: 'my two ouzos for €20 turned into €400. They were kind and dropped it to €200.' The scam targets solo travelers and couples equally, and the 'friendly local' is always a recruiter paid on commission per victim delivered. These bars have no posted menus and no Google Maps presence because the few reviews they have are one-star scam warnings. Older travelers sometimes feel this couldn't happen to them — the 'friendly local' is often positioned as a retired schoolteacher or a shop owner rather than a young tout, making the approach feel socially legitimate. But the pattern is identical regardless of the recruiter's age. Your protection is simple: a real Athenian never invites a visitor for drinks at an unfamiliar bar. If you want to enjoy an ouzo in Plaka, walk into a named, posted-price ouzeri with good Google reviews — Brettos (the oldest distillery in Athens, transparent pricing), Klimataria, or Ta Karamanlidika tou Fani are community-respected. Pay for each drink as you order it rather than running a tab, and if a 'friendly local' insists you accompany them somewhere, politely decline and walk back to a busy main street.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline any drink invitation from a stranger — a real Athenian does not invite tourists to unfamiliar bars Stick to named, posted-price ouzeria with Google Maps reviews: Brettos, Klimataria, Ta Karamanlidika tou Fani Ask to see the drink list with prices before ordering, and walk out if the bar cannot produce one Pay for each drink at the bar as you order rather than running a tab If the bill is inflated and staff block you, calmly call Tourist Police 171 — venues fold quickly at the mention of police
scams.location: Plaka restaurant rows, Monastiraki side streets, Psyri bars, Athinas Street near Omonia

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet & Rose Distraction Theft
scams.description: You are crossing Syntagma Square toward the Parliament building when a man steps in front of you, grabs your wrist with warm enthusiasm, and ties a colorful 'friendship bracelet' before you can pull back. He smiles, gestures at the bracelet, and demands €10, €20, sometimes €50. If you try to return it he refuses to untie it and raises his voice until you pay to escape the awkwardness. r/GreeceTravel '7 days in Naxos with my girlfriend' (comments/1sgosgy) is blunt: 'Don't let anyone put a friendship bracelet on your wrist. It's a scam — they will hound you for money.' The crew operates in teams of two or three: one ties the bracelet while a partner blocks your escape and 'confirms' it is legitimate. A more alarming variant emerged in 2025. r/GreeceTravel posted a distraction-theft warning titled 'Rose Scam used as a Pickpocket technique' (comments/1oecvk4) about the Psiri area near Little Kook: a vendor places a rose in your hand while an accomplice lifts your wallet from your back pocket during the hug-style contact. Older travelers are particularly targeted because the 'gift' framing makes the interaction feel socially legitimate. The rose is worth cents; the wallet typically has €50–€300 cash and several cards that require urgent cancellation. Both variants cluster at Syntagma Square metro exits, Monastiraki Square, the bottom of Plaka near Hadrian's Arch, and along Ermou shopping street. In August peak season the crews rotate multiple times a day. Your protection is physical and decisive. If someone approaches with a bracelet or flower in hand, cross your arms immediately, step back, and say 'no' firmly. Do not engage in conversation, do not make eye contact, and do not slow your pace. If a bracelet is already on your wrist, walk to a nearby café and cut it off — do not pay anything. If the crew escalates, say 'astynomia' (police) loudly; Tourist Police 171 patrols Syntagma on foot during summer evenings and these crews disperse at the mention.
scams.avoidance: Cross your arms and step back the moment anyone with a bracelet or flower approaches you Do not engage in any conversation — a brief 'no' and continued walking defeats the scam If a bracelet is already on your wrist, walk to a café and cut it off with scissors — do not pay Keep your wallet in a front zipped pocket or a crossbody bag worn in front, not a back pocket Say 'astynomia' loudly if the crew escalates; Syntagma has summer Tourist Police foot patrol
scams.location: Syntagma Square, Monastiraki flea market, Plaka entrance, Ermou shopping street, Psyri at dusk

scams.name: Fake Police 'ID Check' Pickpocket
scams.description: Two men in plain clothes approach on a Metro platform or on the walk from your cruise ship in Piraeus. They flash what looks like a police identification card and say they need to check for counterfeit euros, or to verify your passport. While you fumble for your wallet, one of them scans the contents while the other distracts you with questions. You hand the wallet back; an hour later you realize €150 is missing and your credit card number has been photographed. Real Greek police do not stop-check tourist wallets on the street. r/greece 'Does the police have the right to ask for your personal' (comments/1oa974y) confirms that even genuine officers verify identification via headquarters rather than inspecting documents on-the-spot. Omonia Square Metro station has drawn the most concentrated warnings from the US Embassy in Athens since 2023. The station is a Metro transfer hub with constant tourist flow from the airport line to the central line, and disorientation is high. r/GreeceTravel 'Any unsafe places in Athens/Santorini/Mykonos' (comments/1fo8ej1) captures the local advice: 'You should beware of pickpockets and scammers all the time. If you use taxis, then use Uber.' A parallel variant involves someone offering help with your bags at the station steps — while your back is turned lifting a suitcase, a partner opens the outer pocket of the bag on the floor and removes your phone. Cruise passengers arriving at Piraeus are targeted specifically because they often carry multiple cards, passports, and cash in a day-bag that was convenient on-ship. The fake-officer team knows cruise arrivals have to meet a tour bus or onward transfer within an hour, creating time pressure that makes tourists comply faster. Your protection: real Greek police always wear uniforms, and if a plain-clothes officer genuinely needs to speak to you they will invite you to walk to the nearest police station together. If asked to open your wallet on the street, refuse firmly, say you will call 112 (general emergency) or 171 (Tourist Police), and walk to the nearest open shop or café. Fake officers always disperse at the threat of a real phone call.
scams.avoidance: Real Greek police do not spot-check tourist wallets on the street — always refuse and walk away If genuine police stop you, they wear uniforms; offer to walk with them to the nearest police station Avoid Omonia Square at night and in early morning hours when tourist pickpocket activity peaks Keep your passport in the hotel safe; carry a photocopy and minimal cards only If accosted, say loudly 'I am calling 112' — fake officers disperse immediately
scams.location: Metro stations (Omonia, Monastiraki, Syntagma), near bus stops, Acropolis perimeter, Piraeus port

scams.name: Plaka & Monastiraki Tourist-Menu Restaurant Overcharge
scams.description: You sit down for lunch at a Plaka taverna with a view of the Roman Agora. You order moussaka, a Greek salad, and two glasses of wine. Bread and olives arrive — unrequested — and a small plate of tzatziki. The bill totals €95. At the table, an expanded menu appears with different prices than the one posted outside: the moussaka was €24 (typical Athens price is €12), the salad €18 (typical €8), and the 'welcome' items total €14. r/greece 'Suggestions for a walk and dinner in Athens' (comments/1kf89ek) is clear: 'Don't go to the touristy restaurants in Plaka near the ancient ruins, because they'll overcharge you for mediocre food.' r/travel 'Tips from a Greek for people visiting Greece' (comments/voxqy8) adds: 'Before buying stuff at a restaurant, be very careful of the prices on the list. If there are no prices, chances are you're in a tourist trap.' The mechanic is opaque pricing plus 'optional' extras that arrive unordered. Restaurants in Plaka, around Monastiraki Square, and on the Acropolis slope often serve bread, olives, tzatziki, and sometimes a small ouzo 'as a welcome' — each appearing on the bill at €3–€15. The menu at the entrance may show lower prices than the one at the table, and the staff may bring items 'because it is traditional' without announcing charges. Older travelers with limited Greek are particularly vulnerable because the items feel like generous hospitality rather than upsells. Your protection: read the menu at the entrance before sitting, and confirm prices at the table match when the menu arrives. Decline any 'welcome' items explicitly when they arrive — 'ochi, efcharisto' (no thank you) is enough, or simply wave them off with a polite smile. Count the bill line by line against the menu you ordered from, and dispute any cover charge or service charge not listed on the menu. For genuine Greek food at local prices, walk one block away from the main tourist spine: Koukaki (south of the Acropolis), Pangrati (east of the National Garden), and Exarchia (north of Syntagma) all have well-reviewed, honestly-priced tavernas. Scholarchio and Platanos in Plaka itself are community-respected for honest pricing.
scams.avoidance: Read the menu at the entrance before sitting, and confirm prices at the table match when the menu arrives Decline 'welcome' items explicitly when they arrive — 'ochi, efcharisto' politely refused Eat one block away from Plaka's main rows — Koukaki, Pangrati, Exarchia have fair-priced authentic tavernas Use Google Maps reviews (4.3+, 200+ reviews) to find honest Plaka options: Scholarchio, Platanos Count the bill line by line and dispute any charge not on the menu you ordered from
scams.location: Plaka (Adrianou and Kydathinaion streets), Monastiraki Square perimeter, Acropolis slope restaurants

scams.name: Metro & Tour-Bus Pickpocket Teams
scams.description: The Athens Metro is otherwise clean and safe, but two corridors see concentrated pickpocket activity: Line 3 between Syntagma and the airport (where tourists load on with luggage), and Omonia station more generally. Teams operate in three- or four-person groups — one distracts, one lifts, one receives the wallet, one keeps lookout. The 2024 and 2025 Ekathimerini reporting on organized Athens theft networks confirms the pattern is larger than individual opportunists. r/GreeceTravel 'Any unsafe places in Athens/Santorini/Mykonos' (comments/1fo8ej1) is the community baseline. The most common patterns targeting older travelers: a fake crowd crush at carriage doors where someone pushes you from behind while another reaches into your jacket pocket; a 'map distraction' where someone asks for directions with a large open map blocking your view of your bag; and an escalator bump where a passenger 'falls' into you at the top or bottom while a partner lifts. The Acropolis ticket queue is another hotspot — lines can stretch to 200 people in peak summer, and teams circulate pretending to be fellow tourists. Tour buses at Syntagma have their own problem: when a group is loading luggage, someone helps lift bags while a partner opens day-bags set on the sidewalk. The damage is typically a phone (€500–€1,200 replacement for a current iPhone) or a wallet (€50–€300 cash plus several hours of card cancellation). For insurance documentation, reporting to Tourist Police 171 within 24 hours is essential. Your protection: wear a zipped crossbody bag in front of you in any crowded environment; never use an outer backpack pocket for valuables; split cash across multiple pockets (some in a money belt or inner jacket pocket, some in your front trouser pocket, none in a back pocket); do not pull out your phone on crowded escalators or at carriage doors. When waiting at the Acropolis ticket queue, keep your bag in front of you and your hand on it; if you are on an organized tour, ask your guide to watch your bag while you photograph the monuments.
scams.avoidance: Wear a zipped anti-theft crossbody bag in front of you in any crowded environment Keep phone in a zipped inner pocket or zipped jacket pocket, never in a back pocket Split cash: €20 in a front pocket, the rest in a money belt or hotel safe Do not pull out your phone on crowded escalators, at carriage doors, or on Line 3 during rush hour Report any theft to Tourist Police 171 within 24 hours for insurance documentation
scams.location: Metro Line 3 (airport to Syntagma), Omonia transfer station, Acropolis queue, tour buses at Syntagma

scams.name: Hotel & Booking Off-Platform Payment Fraud
scams.description: You book a highly-rated hotel in Koukaki on Booking.com, with a clear view of the Acropolis. The reservation confirms at €180 per night. Three days before your trip an email arrives that looks official, claiming 'to finalize your booking, please pay the deposit through this secure link.' The link looks similar to Booking.com but is a fake. You pay €540 for three nights. On arrival, the actual hotel has no record of your reservation — the original Booking.com reservation was cancelled when you 'paid directly.' r/GreeceTravel 'Booked a hotel directly. 24 hours later they emailed a link' (comments/1rf3s8b) documents this pattern. r/travel 'How I was scammed on booking and WhatsApp' (comments/115ignt) confirms that scammers infiltrate the booking.com message system itself. The Athens-specific version clusters around Koukaki (Acropolis adjacent, high demand), central Plaka, and Syntagma. Operators also create lookalike property listings — r/Santorini 'Scam alert A&G Suites' (comments/1kn5wxv) shows the parallel pattern on Santorini ('anything else with the same pictures like A&G is a scam'). The Athens version runs year-round because demand is constant. Older travelers are targeted specifically because the scammers count on careful planners who book well in advance and respond quickly to official-looking emails. Your protection starts before arrival. Book only through Booking.com, Hotels.com, Expedia, or the hotel's own verified website — never respond to 'payment link' emails, even if they appear to come from Booking.com. Real Booking.com transactions occur inside the app or on the booking.com domain (check the URL bar carefully). If you receive a payment request email, log into your Booking.com account separately (not through the email link) and check your reservation status. Call the hotel directly through the phone number listed on Google Maps (not the number in the suspicious email) to verify. Pay only by credit card — this gives you chargeback protection for 60–120 days in most jurisdictions. For peak season (April–October) at popular Athens hotels, book eight or more weeks ahead through official channels to reduce exposure to last-minute 'deal' scams.
scams.avoidance: Book only through Booking.com, Hotels.com, Expedia, or the hotel's own verified website Never click payment links in emails; log into your booking account directly and check reservation status Call the hotel through the Google Maps phone number (not the email's number) to verify any payment request Pay only by credit card — chargeback is your strongest protection For peak season (April–October), book eight or more weeks ahead through official channels
scams.location: Citywide — advertised as Plaka, Koukaki (Acropolis view), Kolonaki, central Syntagma
